aiOverview.content: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are new, tax-advantaged investment accounts for children under 18, offering a federal $1,000 "seed" contribution for children born between 2025 and 2028. Parents can open these accounts to invest up to $5,000 annually in US stock index funds, with funds tax-deferred until age 18 for, e.g., education or housing. Key details about the Trump Accounts for Kids: Purpose: To build early wealth for children through stock market investments, often referred to as "baby bonds". Eligibility & Funding: Children born between Jan 1, 2025, and Dec 31, 2028, qualify for an initial $1,000 from the government, notes WHYY and this YouTube video confirm. Investment Limits: Families can contribute up to $5,000 annually per child, notes ERS Texas (.gov) and this YouTube video. How to Open: Parents can file IRS Form 4547 during the 2026 tax season for children born in 2025. Usage: Funds are locked until the child turns 18 and are intended for expenses such as higher education or a first-time home purchase, notes the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video. Account Access: While accounts can be requested via tax forms, an official enrollment portal is set to launch in summer 2026, says the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video. These accounts, designed to operate similarly to IRAs, must be invested in low-cost US stock index mutual funds or ETFs, according to ERS Texas (.gov) and this YouTube video.
